title: Technology dependency and its forecast — what would unblock the work, and when
_role: Every TECH-* and FC-* validates against the corresponding $def. A TECH-* sits between a blocker and a scan trigger: BLK-* <-retired by- TECH-* -dated by-> FC-*, and TRG-* detects it.

name.description: What has to exist, in words a literature search could use.

category.description: `experimental_access` is not a technology and is deliberately here anyway: it behaves exactly like one -- external, watched for, retires named blockers, has a plausible arrival -- and the alternative is that the highest-fan-out non-method dependency in the portfolio has nowhere to live.

why_it_matters.description: What changes about THIS program if it lands. Not what it means for the field.

current_state.description: `partially_landed` is a real state and matters: a capability can arrive for one arm of what a route needs and not another. Recording a half-arrival as `landed` licences claims the tool does not support; recording it as `absent` wastes the arm that did arrive.

evidence.description: What the current_state assessment rests on -- a released tool, a benchmark, a deposit. REQUIRED non-empty for any state other than `absent`, and for `partially_landed` it must say which half landed.

confidence.description: In the ASSESSMENT of current_state -- not in the arrival, which is the forecast's job.

scan_trigger.description: POINTS at research/method-watch-triggers.json, which is the ONE HOME of the search queries. This register never copies a query. A TECH-* with an EMPTY scan_trigger is flagged in the generated view -- an unscanned dependency is a capability that could land without anyone noticing.

not_scannable_because.description: The ONE legitimate answer to [T3] other than a real query: this capability cannot be detected by a literature search, and here is what watches it instead. ⛔ IT EXISTS TO STOP A FABRICATED QUERY. TECH-COMPUTE-COST is 'a sustained fall in the cost per nanosecond of the simulation we actually buy' -- that is measured from a live market board by relaunch_market_gate.price_offers and vast_cost_model.py, and inventing an arXiv query for a GPU price would manufacture exactly the credited-but-silent scanner MAINTENANCE.md section 4 warns about. Mirrors `not_searchable_because` in the trigger register, deliberately: one vocabulary for one idea.

fan_out.description: DERIVED: how many routes, requirements and instruments this would reopen. Orders the watch list.

pending_signals.description: Literature hits the weekly scan matched against this technology's TRG-* queries and that NOBODY HAS GRADED YET. ⛔ THE SCAN WRITES ONLY HERE. It never touches `current_state`, `evidence` or the forecast — its own contract is that every hit is an unvalidated lead and nothing may change a status by itself, and an auto-updating register would break the one rule that keeps the watch list honest. Grading is a human edit: read the paper, then promote it into `evidence[]`, move `current_state`, and re-date the forecast.

graded.description: Set true by a human once read. An ungraded signal is surfaced in the generated view and warned on by the checker; it is a QUEUE, not a claim.

scenarios.description: The three must be genuinely different. If conservative and optimistic land in the same window, either the capability is nearly here or the forecast has not been thought about -- both need saying.

expected_impact.description: Grades what it changes HERE, not in the field. A capability can be a major general advance and marginal for this program.

basis.description: MANDATORY. An unlabelled forecast is indistinguishable from a measurement. `speculative` is legitimate and is not a failure -- the alternative to a labelled guess is not a better number, it is silence, and silence about a two-year horizon defaults the program to a conservative answer without ever saying so.

what_would_move_this.description: What observation would shift the expected band. Makes the forecast falsifiable rather than decorative.

adoption_note.description: A method existing in a paper, existing as usable software, and being validated on THIS regime are three different arrival dates. date_band refers to the third, because that is the one that unblocks work here.

last_reviewed.description: REQUIRED. A forecast older than two quarters is flagged in the generated view rather than silently trusted.

date_band.description: A half-year or year window, never a point date. `never` is valid only where the scenario genuinely rules the capability out.
